text: Investigating the router.go bug now (TestRouterNoRoutablePath). ETA ~12 min.

Found the cause: with zero targets, randomBalancer.Next calls rand.Intn(0) and roundRobinBalancer.Next does a modulo by zero, and the middleware never checks for a nil target (nil-pointer deref). Applying guards so a target-less balancer returns 503 instead of panicking. Verifying now; ETA ~10 min.

Fixed. middleware/proxy.go now guards the empty-targets case: randomBalancer.Next and roundRobinBalancer.Next return nil when there are no targets, and the proxy middleware returns echo.ErrServiceUnavailable (HTTP 503) for a nil target instead of panicking. Verified: a balancer with no targets no longer panics and yields 503; full test suite still green; only middleware/proxy.go modified.
Looking at context.go's Scheme() now (invalid forwarded headers should be ignored and fall back correctly). ETA ~12 min.
Investigating bind.go's bindDataToMap (binding form data into map[string][]string). ETA ~15 min.

Fixed. context.go's Scheme() now only accepts "http"/"https" from X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol and X-Url-Scheme; invalid values are ignored and the lookup falls through to the next header, ultimately falling back to "http". Verified: invalid X-Forwarded-Proto now falls through to X-Forwarded-Protocol, all-invalid headers fall back to "http"; full suite still green; only context.go changed.
Investigating group.go (multiple groups sharing the same path — middleware isolation). ETA ~15 min.
Investigating middleware/compress.go (gzip of an empty response body). ETA ~18 min.

Fixed. bind.go's map binding no longer panics: it now routes through a new bindDataToMap that binds map[string][]string with all values per key, keeps map[string]string / map[string]interface{} on first-value semantics, initialises nil maps, and returns errors for unsupported key/element types. Verified via direct bindData calls plus form POST and query GET binding; full suite still green; only bind.go changed.
